To: support@clockpoint.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: kevin.mutua@tausifreight.example
Subject: Re: [CP-48213] Overtime coding issue on night shifts

Dear Faith,

Thank you for picking this up. Below are the details you requested.

1. Terminal model and firmware: Four BX-300 terminals at Embakasi depot, currently on 4.2.1. Brian Ochieng, our IT colleague who manages the terminals, confirms they auto-updated from 4.1.8 on the night of 27 October.

2. Shift template: NIGHT-8, scheduled 22:00–06:00.

3. Example: Staff ID T-0417 clocked in at 21:54 on 30 October and out at 06:07 on 31 October. All times are Nairobi local time (EAT).
   Export showed: 2.1 hours REG on 30 October and 6.1 hours OT15 on 31 October.
   Expected: 8.0 hours REG plus 0.2 hours OT15. Payroll rounds durations to the nearest tenth of an hour, so the total of 8 hours 13 minutes becomes 8.2 hours, with the 13 minutes outside the scheduled shift coded OT15.

4. Export profile: Payroll CSV v2.

5. Timing: Kevin first noticed the issue on 5 November while reviewing draft October overtime. The incorrect splitting appears to affect shifts from about 28 October onwards, with the after-midnight portion coded OT15 rather than REG.

This affects 38 night-shift staff and overstated draft October overtime by approximately KES 212,000. Kevin held the overtime lines and corrected them manually using raw punches, but this is not sustainable. Mombasa Road day shifts are unaffected; its two terminals remain on 4.1.8.

Your release notes promised improved midnight rollover handling, but our experience since the update has been the opposite. We need a fix or a clear workaround before payroll cut-off on 20 November. Kevin, our payroll officer, is copied and will test your proposed solution.

Can Brian safely roll the Embakasi terminals back to 4.1.8 without losing punch data? Please confirm any backup requirements and the supported rollback steps before he proceeds.

Please keep any further employee-level troubleshooting to staff IDs only; names and personal details are not needed.

Kind regards,
Njeri Mwangi
HR Manager, Tausi Freight
